detail: The licence, version, embargo and access status live in the Zenodo repository record, not in the deposited file. Nothing in pkg/ can confirm or refute them; a verifier must open https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10522812 and read the record.
24 of about 30 reported variables are identified, 6 remain ambiguous, none is unlocatable.
Table 3 is a resubstitution matrix, not a cross-validated one.

The comment's 'Information gain, unweighted = 42.5 laps' row is not checkable as written: the comment does not say which analytic sample produced it, and on the sample the rest of the table uses this pipeline gets a different value. 42.5 is recoverable only on an alternative sample definition (all predictors, at most three missing) that the comment does not name.

The leaf-count triple 7 / 11 / 15 is not reproducible from the settings the comment states. Under Gini with the stated depth cap of 5 and minimum leaf of 5, this pipeline gets 8 leaves at the silent complexity default and 8 with no penalty under default priors, against the comment's 7 and 11; 15 under balanced priors with no penalty does reproduce. The triple is recoverable only by also varying minsplit, which the comment does not report -- which is, ironically, the very defect the claim is about.
A permuted-outcome null shows the observed in-sample fit is barely outside what the procedure produces on random labels.

The comment's range '90 to 227 children' for the regrown subsample is not reproducible as stated, because the comment does not say what set of regrowths it ranged over; the 300 bootstrap regrowths run here span a wider interval, and a configuration grid spans wider still. The checkable core -- that no regrowth lands on the published 218 -- is checked above. The further clause 'the published second-tree node sizes miss by up to 34 children' additionally requires forcing the subsample, which needs the ambiguous column assignments and the second tree's predictor set, and no code was deposited.
Five of the eleven distinct split variables in the published trees cannot be identified in the deposit at all.
A root-to-leaf sequence in a classification tree has no temporal content, so the title's and Discussion's path, trajectory and spiral language is not supported by the design.

That the prose names three of the five conditions, and that the dropped one is the second weekend-sedentary split at 458 minutes, is read from the article's Discussion. The deposit contains no prose; a verifier must read the paper. The figure side of the claim -- five conditions on the path -- is checked above from the transcribed tree.

The two interpretive passages are about children reaching node 16 and node 21 of the SECOND tree, and the second tree does not reproduce (C-5.4): its subsample cannot be recovered without knowing which of the ambiguous column assignments the authors used, and two of the conditions on the path to node 16 -- satisfaction of the need for relatedness, and perceived competence in stability -- are among the five split variables that cannot be identified in the deposit at all (C-5.5).

The software statement is a sentence in the article's Methods. The deposit contains no script, no seed, no session information and no package manifest, so nothing in pkg/ can confirm or refute it; a verifier reads the paper. That the deposit contains none of those things IS checkable and is checked in C-A1.
Ten of twenty-nine analytic decisions are stated unambiguously, three are verifiable from the deposit, and none is verifiable as executed.
The archive is simultaneously too open and too closed: maximal individual-level detail released without restriction, with no codebook to make that detail usable.

That no participant NAME appears anywhere in the package is an absence, and establishing it requires knowing which tokens are participant names and which are the authors' -- a judgement the comment made by testing each candidate token against the published article. This notebook deliberately does not print or pattern-match name-like strings from the deposit, because doing so in a verification artefact would republish exactly what the comment asks the authors to remove. The structural half of the claim -- no hidden sheets, no formulas, no external links, one comment part -- is checked above.

The repository record's collection window (2019-2022, four consecutive years) against the paper's stated academic year 2022-2023, and the fact that the deposit predates the paper's submission, are properties of the Zenodo record and the article, neither of which is inside pkg/.

Every element of the consent claim is an absence in the ARTICLE and in the Zenodo record: no mention of child assent, no data-protection or retention statement, no disclosure-control statement, no operational definition of 'anonymized', and no repository-side ethics or restriction statement. Absences in documents that are not in pkg/ cannot be checked from pkg/. A verifier confirms them by full-text search of the article and by opening the repository record.

No re-identification of any child was attempted, no external register was consulted, and no threat-model assessment was performed; every figure in Section 8 is a distribution or a count, so what is established is a demonstrated capability rather than a demonstrated harm.

Six of the map's rows are marked confidence B or C: parental versus peer support, which basic-psychological-need subscale is relatedness, which of two deposited administrations of an instrument was used, and which of four minute-scaled columns are the two sedentary variables.

Three clauses of this paragraph are not checked here: the 23 Likert sums below their own arithmetic minimum and the 16 height decreases across consecutive waves both require the per-instrument item counts and the wave alignment the audit reconstructed by hand, and the response-scale change from seven to five points between waves 2 and 3 requires knowing which header is the same instrument across waves. None changes a published number and the comment says so.
The abstract's '24 of about 30 reported variables' is the classification judgement of C-2.4, carried into the abstract unchanged.

Which findings count as changing a published CONCLUSION rather than a published VALUE is a reading of the comment's own labelling, not a computation on the deposit. The four labelled 'yes' are listed in the chunk; a verifier counting Section 6 as a fifth would not be wrong, and the abstract handles it as a separate clause.
